newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, China may set up joint cargo airline.
newsitem.headline: Russia, China may set up joint cargo airline.

text.p: Senior Russian and Chinese aviation officials next week will discuss a plan to set up a joint cargo airline, a spokesman for private Russian cargo carrier Volga-Dnepr said on Thursday.

The spokesman, Konstantin Rogov, said Volga-Dnepr Chief Executive Alexei Isaykin planned to travel to China with a delegation headed by First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov. The visit will begin on June 23.
"Our Chinese partner is very interested in setting up the joint cargo airline, which will carry cargo inside China and service cargo routes between China and Russia," Rogov said.
Viktor Gorlov, deputy head of Russian Federal Aviation Service (FAS), told Reuters that FAS supported the idea of establishing the company.
"We see this project as mutually promising," he said.
In April, Russian Transport Minister Nikolai Tsakh visited China to discuss the project, but Russian officials declined to comment on the results of the talks.
Rogov said Volga-Dnepr's partner -- China's State Aviation Corp -- was keen on setting up the company. "But they are waiting for the Chinese government's approval of this idea," he added.
Rogov also said the new company, which does not yet have a name, planned to operate Russian-made Ilyushin-76 and Tupolev Tu-204C freighters to service scheduled and charter flights.
"These planes will be leased," he added. He did not say how many aircraft were involved.

Volga-Dnepr makes scheduled cargo flights from Ulyanovsk in central Russia to three destinations in China, operating heavy Antonov An-124s and Ilyushin Il-76s. They carry mostly consumer goods and home electronics to Russia as well as heavy machinery to China.
The company's 1996 sales volume on flights to and from China was $11.7 million, compared with $10 million the previous year.
Last year, Volga-Dnepr carried a total 45,000 tonnes of cargo, or 13 percent of Russia's total air cargo turnover, second only to Aeroflot.
